messages:
maya: CI is red on a weird nondet unit test in runtime serving: TestRetryTimerSignal. Fails ~1-3% in CI, looks timing-related. Can someone triage when they have a minute?

devops-bot: CI failure: https://ci.internal/redwood/job/serve-runtime/4872 — failing step: unit-tests (linux). Attached logs. rerun available with :retry: command.

chris: thanks. any repro locally? seed or env we can use to increase hit rate?

maya: i ran `bazel test //runtime/serve:test_retry_timer --runs_per_test=100` and hit it twice. command i used: `TEST_SEED=42 BAZEL_FLAGS=--test_arg=--run_flaky ./bazelisk test //runtime/serve:test_retry_timer --runs_per_test=100`

lee: paste of the failing snippet:
```
--- FAIL: TestRetryTimerSignal (0.12s)
    retry_test.go:87: expected retry triggered before backoff expired, got timeout
    log: timer fired at 123ms, expected ~100ms +/- jitter
```

sam: looks like the test assumes deterministic scheduling. maybe flaky under CI cpus. two quick options: mock time (preferred) or widen assertion tolerance. both are fine short-term.

chris: agree. can we get a rerun to see if it's reproducible in CI now? i'll kick one if maya can't.

maya: kicked rerun — devops-bot should post status.

devops-bot: Rerun queued: job 4890. ETA ~5m.

qa-bot: suggestion: add flaky annotation to the test so it doesn't block release while we fix. tag: @flaky(tolerance=3) or platform equivalent.

lee: i'd prefer a minimal fix: add deterministic clock mock in retry_test.go and a fixed jitter source. I'll pick this up unless someone objects.

sam: +1 to deterministic clock. also add a small regression test around jitter bounds.

chris: sounds good. maya — can you drop the exact run command and seed that reproduced it into the issue? will help bisect if needed.

maya: done — added comment to https://git.internal/redwood/serve-runtime/issues/314 with the `TEST_SEED=42` steps and two failing log snippets.

devops-bot: Rerun finished: job 4890 — flaky test still failed (1/1).

maya: confirmed CI rerun still failed. attaching full failure trace in the issue.

lee: ok i'll open a PR with the mocked clock + deterministic jitter and a small note in the test that it was flaky on CI. PR will include a TODO to remove mock if we refactor scheduler.

sam: tagging chris as reviewer. chris can you take a quick look once lee opens?

chris: will do. quick nit: when you mock clock, also assert no real sleeping (no `time.Sleep`) left behind. those sneaky sleeps hide flakiness.

maya: thanks everyone. assigning follow-ups: lee -> implement mock + PR, chris -> review, sam -> add flaky annotation if PR is delayed, maya -> continue to collect seeds and logs. :thumbsup:

lee: grabbing it now. ETA for PR by end of day. :eyes:

sam: if you want faster validation, add a CI presubmit job with `--runs_per_test=50` for that test only. reduces noise before merge.

lee: good call. will add that to the PR.

chris: perfect. once PR merges, we can remove the flaky tag if it stabilizes.

qa-bot: reminder: file a postmortem note in the tests backlog if this is >3 CI flakes in the past 30 days.

maya: noted. I'll update the backlog after we confirm fixes.

sam: thx folks, keeping this thread for follow-ups. :partyparrot:
